sections.heading: C — License requirements, identification and learner licenses
sections.markdown:
## C — License requirements, identification and learner licenses

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A07
Every Alabama resident who drives a motor vehicle needs a driver license, except when temporarily moving a farm tractor or implement of husbandry on a road. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A07
Anyone never licensed in Alabama, or whose Alabama license expired more than three years ago, must pass the driver exam; an out-of-state license expired one year or less needs no exam. [A07]
Why it matters: the three-year and one-year cutoffs apply to different licenses and are easy to swap.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A07
A federal employee driving a vehicle owned or leased by the U.S. government needs no Alabama license for that driving. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A07
A resident aged 16 or older carrying a valid home-state or home-country license may drive without an Alabama one, including out-of-state military families stationed here on long assignments. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A07
A non-resident aged 16 or older from a country that does not license drivers may drive here up to 90 days per calendar year if the vehicle is registered for the current year at home. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A07
A new resident with a valid license from the previous state may drive on it for 30 days after moving to Alabama. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A07
A non-resident full-time student enrolled at an Alabama school, college or trade school may drive on a valid home license. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A08
Alabama will not license anyone under 16, anyone suspended or revoked in any state, or anyone who fails a required exam. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A08
A license is also refused to a habitual drunkard or narcotics addict, or to someone whose physical or mental impairment, in the view of ALEA or the examiner, would prevent ordinary control of a vehicle. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A08
Applicants under 19 must meet Alabama Act 93-368, which calls for secondary school graduation or current attendance, with limited exclusions. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A08
Every applicant for an original Alabama license or ID card must prove authorized presence in the United States under federal law. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A08
For identification you bring two documents with at least one bearing a photo, or three non-photo documents, and either way one must be from the Primary Listing. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A08
To transfer an out-of-state license you show that license, a Social Security card or other accepted number proof, and one more Primary Listing document. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A09
A prior Alabama license or ID record can prove your birth date; without one, only an original or certified Primary Listing document is accepted. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A09
Only originals or agency-certified copies are accepted, and a certified copy must carry an original certification. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A09
A document is rejected when key details show white-out, erasures or alterations, are missing or unreadable, are hidden by a fold, tear, hole or staple, or when it is not properly signed. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A09
Social Security number proof is needed for any license class, renewal, vessel license or ID card unless the number is on file, even if you do not want it printed. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A09
That proof must be an original showing all 9 digits, such as the card, a certified Social Security Administration letter, form DD 214, a W2, or a Medicare or Medicaid card whose number ends in A. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A10
A notarized document needs a readable seal or stamp, the notary's readable name, a signature, the state of commission, and a commission expiration date still current when notarized. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A10
Immigration documents must show at least 30 days of permitted stay remaining in the United States. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A10
Every applicant under 19 must bring a current Student Enrollment/Exclusion Form, DL-1-93, signed by authorized staff and available at schools or license offices. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A10
Primary documents include a certified U.S. birth certificate, an unexpired U.S. passport, an Alabama license or ID, a naturalization or citizenship certificate, and a valid foreign passport with a U.S. immigration document. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A10
Every 15-year-old applicant must show a certified U.S. birth certificate, and a foreign birth certificate must be translated into English and embassy-certified unless the person has a U.S. passport. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A10
Secondary documents include a marriage license, a military ID or DD-214, a school photo ID, a certified school record, and court decrees such as divorce, adoption or name change. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A11
Written exams are offered in Arabic, Chinese, Farsi, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Thai and Vietnamese. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A11
An applicant unable to read and understand the knowledge test may take an oral exam, which the automated testing equipment can deliver. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A11
Non-citizens may add documents such as an Employment Authorization Document with a valid Social Security card, a visa allowing more than 30 days of stay, or a valid I-94 record. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A11
Alabama's graduated license law took effect October 1, 2002, and the minimum driving age is 16, with certain exceptions and restrictions. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A11
At 15 you can earn a restricted Learner License by passing an exam drawn from this manual, giving a Class D license with a Y restriction. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A11
Before age 16 a Y-restricted learner drives only with a licensed Alabama driver aged 21 or older, or a licensed or certified instructor, in the seat beside them. [A11]
Why it matters: learners often think any licensed adult will do, but before sixteen the companion must be at least twenty-one or an instructor.
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A11
After the sixteenth birthday any licensed driver may sit beside the learner, and the license issued at 15 lasts four years and can be renewed once. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A12
A Learner License earned at 16 or older also carries the Y restriction, requiring a licensed driver beside you, and is valid for four years. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A12
A Learner License can be suspended or revoked for the same causes as a driver license, and also revoked for breaking its own terms. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A12
A driver from 16 to under 18 may take the road test after holding a learner license, including a comparable out-of-state one, for six months or until turning 18. [A12]
Why it matters: the six-month holding period is the gate to the road test for drivers under eighteen.
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A12
You surrender the learner license at the road test, and passing removes the Y restriction for the rest of the four-year period at no cost. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A12
At 14 or 15 you can get a Class M license with a B restriction for a motor driven cycle of at most 200 pounds and 150cc engine displacement. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A12
From 16 a Class M license covers motorcycles only, meaning vehicles with a rider's seat or saddle built to run on no more than three wheels on the ground, tractors excluded. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A12
The ALEA Director may add restrictions needed for safe driving, such as corrective lenses or mechanical aids, and violating one can cost you the license. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A12
A vessel license is available from age 12 by passing the vessel exam at a license office or showing an approved boating safety course certificate. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0012]

Glossary: Y restriction — the learner condition requiring a qualified licensed companion beside the driver [A11]. Primary Listing — the core identity documents, one of which every applicant presents [A08]. B restriction — a Class M limit to motor driven cycles [A12].
Memory aid: Y for "you are not yet alone" — a Y-restricted driver always needs a licensed companion beside them [A11].
